articles.title: Import AI 469: Science AI; RSI simulator; and Zuck's technological pessimism
articles.author: Jack Clark

zh.thesis: 现在的 AI 已经能在陌生环境里靠好奇心发现隐藏规则，但离创意和自主科研还有距离。
paragraphs: DiG-bench 用 70 个文字小游戏测试 AI 的发现能力，规则和目标都藏起来，只能靠试错去猜。最强模型 Opus 5 在最高难度上成功率只有 20%，人类是 100%。
这些游戏大多不公开，防的就是 AI 背答案。即使这样，模型还能靠探索拿下低档分数，说明它们已经有点「直觉」了。
另一个项目叫 Faraday，用 27B 的小模型指挥大模型补全论文里被挖掉的图表。它能赢过更贵的 GPT-5.5，靠的是自己会挑问题、会定实验预算。
这正合 Zuckerberg 的乐观——他把超级智能当工具，说人人都会有发明超能力。但他没回答更狠的问题：比人更会发明的系统，凭什么只替人干活？
所以真正要盯的不是模型多聪明，而是它会不会自主选择研究方向。哪天 DiG 上人类和 AI 打平，递归自我改进可能就真来了。

en.thesis: Today's AI can discover hidden rules in unfamiliar environments through curiosity, but it is still far from creative and autonomous scientific research.
paragraphs: DiG-bench tests AI's discovery ability with 70 text mini-games, where the rules and goals are hidden and can only be guessed through trial and error. The strongest model, Opus 5, only achieves a 20% success rate on the hardest difficulty, while humans achieve 100%.

Most of these games are not public, precisely to prevent AI from memorizing the answers. Even so, models can still score low-level points through exploration, which shows they have a bit of 'intuition'.

Another project, called Faraday, uses a small 27B model to direct larger models to complete missing charts in papers. It can beat the more expensive GPT-5.5, because it chooses its own questions and sets its own experimental budgets.

This aligns with Zuckerberg's optimism—he treats superintelligence as a tool and says everyone will have the superpower of invention. But he does not answer the harder question: why would a system that is better at inventing only work for humans?

So what we really need to watch is not how smart the models are, but whether they will autonomously choose their own research directions. The day AI matches humans on DiG, recursive self-improvement may truly arrive.

zh.thesis: 安全改善带来的经济繁荣，正让一些长期危险的地方变得安全得多。
paragraphs: 索马里的商机正在爆发。商务部长说生意兴隆，机场周边新建高楼密集，26 层的 Dahab Tower 今年就要开业。就在同一片区域，1993 年美军士兵的尸体曾被拖过街头。
繁荣背后是治安好转。一个从瑞典回来的索马里人开了家咖啡连锁店，生意兴旺。不过攻击减少的原因，政府说是封堵了 al-Shabab，智库学者更归功于 CCTV 普及、警察用 iPad 查车、便衣大量上街。
这些都算不上高科技，却实实在在降低了暴力风险。有了安全感，资金、人才、建筑就跟着回来了。
作者以此推出一个更大的判断：世界上许多危险地区，接下来会安全得多。原因不外乎治安技术扩散、极端组织逐渐被压制。索马里只是第一个显眼的例子。
所以别只盯着战乱新闻，商业活动才是风向标。当一栋摩天大楼能盖在曾经的战场旁边，就说明变化已经在发生。单个案例未必普遍，但值得留意这个趋势。

en.thesis: The economic boom from better security is making some long-dangerous places much safer.
paragraphs: Business is booming in Somalia. The commerce minister says trade is thriving, new high-rises are going up around the airport, and the 26-story Dahab Tower opens this year. In that same area, in 1993, the bodies of American soldiers were dragged through the streets.

Behind the boom is better security. A Somali who returned from Sweden opened a coffee chain, and it is doing well. The government credits the decline in attacks to blocking al-Shabab, while think-tank scholars point more to the spread of CCTV, police using iPads to check vehicles, and plainclothes officers out in force.
None of this is high-tech, but it has genuinely lowered the risk of violence. With safety, money, talent, and construction come back.

The author uses this to make a larger point: many dangerous parts of the world are about to get much safer. The reasons are simply that security technology is spreading and extremist groups are being gradually suppressed. Somalia is just the first visible example.

So don't just watch the war news; commercial activity is the real indicator. When a skyscraper can rise next to what was once a battlefield, change is already happening. One case may not be universal, but the trend is worth watching.

articles.title: Ban on Chinese robots leaves U.S. startups stranded
articles.author: Viola Zhou

zh.thesis: 美国禁用中国机器人，但国内供应链还没建起来，政策可能拖累本土初创企业。
paragraphs: 美国联邦通信委员会把外国机器人列入禁止清单，新模型必须在美国组装，且 65% 的部件按价值算要产自美国，2029 年还要升到 75%。法规没点名中国，但明摆着就是冲着中国来的。
禁令一出，美国机器人初创公司先慌了。中国有全球最全的电子供应链，从传感器到执行器，美国要么买不到，要么贵得离谱。有公司为了赶进度，员工从中国带零件坐飞机回美国。
初创公司大多靠中国原型快速迭代，如今路被堵死。有的把组装线迁到加拿大，但部件还是中国的，照样进不了美国市场。创始人直问：苹果都在中国造，更复杂的机器人怎么可能在美国造？
也不是没人叫好。本土厂商觉得禁令能挡住廉价竞争，把客户和研究者的订单逼过来。但连支持者也承认，光有禁令这根大棒不够，政府得拿补贴和扶持当胡萝卜，不然供应链就是无米之炊。
政策想防患于未然，却误伤了自家幼苗。供应链转移不是一朝一夕的事，在替代方案成型前，禁令只会让美国机器人产业停滞几年。

en.thesis: The U.S. ban on Chinese robots leaves domestic startups stranded, because the supply chain isn't ready and policy may hurt homegrown firms.
paragraphs: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission has put foreign robots on a banned list. New models must be assembled in America, and 65% of components by value must be made in the U.S., rising to 75% by 2029. The rule doesn't name China, but it's clearly aimed at China.

The ban has panicked American robot startups. China has the world's most complete electronics supply chain, from sensors to actuators. American firms either can't buy them or pay outrageous prices. One company, to meet deadlines, had employees carry parts from China on flights back to the U.S.

Startups mostly rely on Chinese prototypes for rapid iteration, and now that path is blocked. Some have moved assembly lines to Canada, but the components are still Chinese, so they can't enter the U.S. market either. Founders ask directly: Apple builds in China, so how can more complex robots be built in America?

Not everyone is unhappy. Local manufacturers see the ban as a way to block cheap competition and force orders from customers and researchers their way. But even supporters admit the stick alone isn't enough. The government needs to offer subsidies and support as a carrot, otherwise the supply chain is like cooking without rice.

The policy aims to prevent future risks, but it hurts local seedlings. Moving the supply chain isn't a overnight task, and before alternatives are ready, the ban will only stall the U.S. robot industry for years.

articles.title: Woke 1 is dead. We’ve learned nothing.
articles.author: Matthew Yglesias

zh.thesis: Woke 1 的教训没有被吸取，因为真正助长它的机制依然存在。
paragraphs: 最近很多人说「Woke 1 当时确实太疯」，但这是一种逃避的话术。他们不愿承认自己做过错事，只想悄悄转向新立场，这对受害者的伤害远远不够。
真正让我记忆深刻的是那些明哲保身的人。他们心里清楚哪些说法是荒谬的，却选择不说出口。比如预算专家知道城市花在警察上的钱不比学校多，但他们保持沉默。
这种沉默是理性的：出头反驳会引火烧身，躲过去反而保住名声。这套激励结构现在仍然存在，它让任何错误观点都可能迅速成为主流，因为没人愿意当那个「扫兴的人」。
如今右翼的反醒运动徒有其表。它只是在反对左翼关心弱者的价值观，却复制了同样的有毒模式：制造恐慌、压制异见、奖励随大流。
所以问题不在于某一届「醒」运动有多荒唐，而在于我们从未建立起对狂热的抵抗力。下次浪潮到来时，同样的人会再次沉默，直到为时已晚。

en.thesis: The lessons of Woke 1 have not been learned, because the mechanisms that fueled it are still in place.
paragraphs: Recently many people say 'Woke 1 was indeed too crazy at the time,' but that is a dodge. They are unwilling to admit they did wrong, and just want to quietly shift to a new stance, which is far from enough for the victims.

What really sticks in my memory are the people who played it safe. They knew in their hearts which claims were absurd, yet chose not to say so. For instance, budget experts knew the city did not spend more on police than on schools, but they kept silent.

This silence is rational: speaking out to rebut would bring trouble to oneself, while keeping out of trouble preserves one's reputation. This incentive structure still exists today, and it lets any wrong idea quickly become mainstream, because no one wants to be the 'party pooper'.

Now the right's anti-woke movement is a sham. It only opposes the left's values of caring for the weak, but replicates the same toxic pattern: stoking fear, silencing dissent, and rewarding conformity.

So the problem is not how absurd a particular 'woke' movement was, but that we never built resilience against zealotry. When the next wave comes, the same people will fall silent again, until it is too late.

articles.title: Epictetus Ran a Better Productivity System Than Any App You’ve Bought
articles.author: JA Westenberg

zh.thesis: 生产力工具的问题在于让你接管一切，而斯多葛哲学告诉我们先问一句：这是不是我的事。
paragraphs: 现代生产力工具都有一个共同的前提：你是个懒惰的差生。它们给你收件箱、数据库、标签，让你把每件东西都变成待办，好像一切都要由你负责。
爱比克泰德是古希腊的斯多葛学者，当过奴隶，在租来的房间里教哲学。他的系统不管收件，先问一个问题：什么是你能管的？
答案是只有你的判断、愿望和决定。别人的项目、情绪、算法、市场，都不在你的管辖范围内。工具却总想让你相信，你看到了就该处理。
但你一旦把东西记录下来，就等于接过了责任。所以他的方法是：先分清是否属于自己。别人的事，可以提一次建议，之后就不是你的了。
所以这套方法不追求更高的处理效率，而是重新定义什么是失败。你办不到的事掉了链子，那不是你的失败。真正该问的是：这是我的事吗？

en.thesis: Productivity tools assume you must handle everything, but Stoic philosophy says to ask first: is this my business?
paragraphs: Modern productivity tools share a common premise: you are a lazy, failing student. They give you inboxes, databases, tags, and turn every little thing into a to-do, as if everything is your responsibility.
Epictetus was an ancient Greek Stoic, a former slave, who taught philosophy from a rented room. His system doesn't manage incoming stuff. It first asks one question: what is within your control?

The answer is: only your judgments, wishes, and decisions. Other people's projects, emotions, algorithms, markets — none of those are under your control. But tools keep making you believe that if you see it, you must deal with it.

Once you write something down, you take ownership. So his method is to first separate what is yours from what isn't. If it's someone else's business, you can offer a suggestion once, after that it's not your problem.
So this approach isn't about processing things more efficiently. It redefines failure. If something you couldn't control slips, that's not your failure. The real question is: is this my business?

articles.title: How a solo founder used Codex and ChatGPT to launch a fashion brand without engineers | Yana Welinder
articles.author: Claire Vo

zh.thesis: 一个没有工程师的创始人，用 AI 当技术搭档，就把一个服装品牌从草图做到了能收钱的电商网站。
paragraphs: Yana Welinder 独自创办了 AI 原生的时装品牌 Yana Bana。她不是工程师，以前做产品管理，但现在她的技术搭档是 Codex 和 ChatGPT。
她的做法是把时尚灵感写成一份详细的技术规格，包括轮廓、面料垂感、甚至走路时的声音。把这个「提示词」喂给 ChatGPT 的图像生成模型，就能得到一致的、逼真的设计图。
更厉害的是她用 Codex 的电脑操作能力去驱动 CLO 3D 这类她从未学过的服装设计软件，直接生成 CAD 文件用于 3D 打印。供应商的寻找、沟通、建站、支付，全流程都靠 AI 完成。
她现在同时测试真人打版师和 Codex，想看看谁做得更好。这不仅是工具演示，更展示了单人创业的新可能——技术不再是门槛。
所以这件事的意义在于，当 AI 能操作软件、能写代码、能跑通商务流程，一个人就能撬动以前需要一个团队才能做的事。真正的限制不再是技能，而是想法和执行力。

en.thesis: A founder with no engineers used AI as her technical partner, taking a fashion brand from sketch to a working e-commerce site.
paragraphs: Yana Welinder is the solo founder of the AI-native fashion brand Yana Bana. She is not an engineer, and her background is in product management, but now her technical partner is Codex and ChatGPT.

Her method is to write a detailed technical specification for her fashion ideas, covering silhouette, fabric drape, even the sound of walking. This 'prompt' is fed to ChatGPT's image generation model, and it produces consistent, realistic design drawings.

What is more impressive is that she uses Codex's computer operation ability to drive CLO 3D, a fashion design software she never learned, and directly generate CAD files for 3D printing. Finding suppliers, communication, building the website, and processing payments — the whole process is handled by AI.

She is currently testing a human pattern maker against Codex to see who does better. This is not just a tool demonstration; it showcases a new possibility for solo entrepreneurship — technology is no longer a barrier.

So the significance here is that when AI can operate software, write code, and handle business processes, one person can leverage what used to require a team. The real limit is no longer skill, but ideas and execution.

articles.title: Pluralistic: Jennifer Jenkins' 'Music Copyright, Creativity, and Culture' (17 Aug 2026)
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

zh.thesis: 现行音乐版权看似自然，其实是层层堆叠的偶然产物，需要一本像 Jenkins 这样的书来拆解。
paragraphs: Jennifer Jenkins 是 Duke 公共领域中心负责人，每年新年盘点进入公共领域的作品。她最擅长把版权这种又复杂又反直觉的法律讲明白，连漫画都用上了。
Jenkins 的新书叫《音乐版权、创造性与文化》，刚出了第二版，开放获取可下载。它把音乐的经济、文化、政治和艺术史编在一起，从古代讲到机械复制时代再到 AI。
书里特别批评了 Ed Sheeran、Katy Perry、Pharrell Williams 那几个案子。法官判「感觉像」算抄袭，这恰恰暴露了音乐版权制度的根本矛盾：面对新技术，规则是东拼西凑出来的。
作者认为，我们今天关于「谁该付钱、什么时候要许可」的常识，并不是自然的，而是一直在变化。过去如此，现在也一样。
整篇文章其实是给这本书做推荐，大量篇幅是链接汇总，书本身只占一小段。真正可带走的观点就是那句：音乐版权制度一团糟，而 Jenkins 把它讲清楚了。

en.thesis: Current music copyright looks natural but is really a pile of accidents, and a book like Jenkins' is needed to take it apart.
paragraphs: Jennifer Jenkins runs the Duke Center for the Public Domain and every New Year she lists the works entering the public domain. She is best at making copyright, a complex and counterintuitive field, clear to laypeople, even using comics.

Her new book is called 'Music Copyright, Creativity, and Culture', and the second edition is out, free to download. It weaves together the economic, cultural, political, and artistic history of music, from ancient times to the mechanical reproduction era and on to AI.

The book is especially critical of the cases involving Ed Sheeran, Katy Perry, and Pharrell Williams. When judges rule that 'feels like' counts as copying, it exposes the root contradiction of music copyright: facing new technology, the rules are patched together from bits and pieces.
The author argues that our current common sense about who should pay and when permission is needed is not natural, but has always been changing. It was true in the past, and it's true now.

The whole article is really a recommendation for the book, with much of the length made up of link roundups, and the book itself taking only a short paragraph. The real takeaway is that line: the music copyright system is a mess, and Jenkins has explained it clearly.

articles.title: Am I better because of AI?
articles.author: dreamreal

zh.thesis: AI 的真正价值不是效率，而是逼着你思考自己是谁、想说什么。
paragraphs: 作者最近参与了一场讨论，主题是怎么才算「有效」使用 AI。但他发现，现在根本没法回头做对照实验，没有 AI 的版本已经不存在了。
所以「有没有变得更好」这个问题，答案无从验证。他承认自己也说不清结果如何。
但他仍觉得 AI 让他变好了：它逼着他去想自己是谁、真正想表达什么。至于怎么表达，AI 帮不上太多忙。
这更像是一种自我认知的工具，而不是效率工具。它不给你答案，只是逼你面对问题。
所以判断 AI 有没有用，可能不该看产出，而该看它有没有逼你想清楚自己要什么。

en.thesis: AI's real value is not efficiency; it forces you to think about who you are and what you want to say.
paragraphs: The author recently joined a discussion about what counts as 'effective' use of AI. But he realized there is no way to run a controlled experiment now, because the version without AI no longer exists.
So the question of whether he has become better is impossible to verify. He admits he cannot say clearly what the result has been.
But he still feels AI has made him better: it forces him to think about who he is and what he truly wants to express. As for how to express it, AI does not help much.
This makes it more a tool for self-knowledge than for efficiency. It does not give you answers; it just forces you to face the questions.
So judging whether AI is useful may not be about the output, but about whether it forces you to think clearly about what you want.
